paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to take from this song. David doesn't open with a plan or a complaint. He opens with "I love You, O LORD, my strength." Then he calls Him his rock, his fortress and his shield, because when David was in trouble, he ran TO the LORD (Psalm 18:1-2).

Now look at how big the rescue is. David says the cords of death were around him and his foes were "too mighty for me," and I think that's the whole point (Psalm 18:4, 17). When he cried out, God heard from His temple and "reached down from on high and took hold of me" (Psalm 18:6, 16). So when you're in over your head, you don't have to get yourself out first. You cry out, and He's the One who reaches down.

And watch what David gives credit to at the end. The strong arms, the quick feet and the won battles all come from God, who "arms me with strength" and whose gentleness lifts him up (Psalm 18:32, 35). The song ends with the LORD showing "loving devotion to His anointed, to David and his descendants forever" (Psalm 18:50). So, baker, go ahead and sing about what He's done for you, and sing it LOUD, because your strength and your rescue were always His.
